title: New snake species from New Guinea named in honor of Slash
subtitle: The species Lielaphis slashi was confirmed through genetic tests and distinct physical characteristics.
excerpt: Scientists have named a newly discovered New Guinea snake Lielaphis slashi, honoring Guns N’ Roses guitarist Slash, a reptile enthusiast since childhood.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Scientists have described and named a newly discovered snake species from New Guinea in honor of Slash, guitarist of the rock band Guns N’ Roses. The musician was chosen because he has loved reptiles since childhood.

The reptile has been formally christened Lielaphis slashi. Confirmation that it represents a species not previously recognized by the scientific community came from comparisons of physical differences and the execution of genetic tests.

Characteristics and habits of the species

Classified as a ground-dwelling snake with a reddish‑brown coloration, Lielaphis slashi is non‑venomous. Morphologically, the animal possesses large posterior teeth that can be used to grasp and capture specific prey such as slippery lizards and reptile eggs.

Biological recognition methodology

The formal recognition process for new animals involves systematic biological analysis methods:

  • Morphological assessment: comparison of external physical and structural traits with already known specimens;
  • Genetic testing: sequencing and contrasting genetic material to prove exclusive evolutionary lineages;
  • Taxonomic nomenclature: formal application of rules to designate the species in scientific literature.

The combined use of genetic examinations and morphological analysis accurately confirms distinctions between similar species within herpetology, enabling the official cataloguing of reptile diversity.

With information from ScienceDaily.
